about: An element of a list variable read by its index, in an assignment, an arithmetic operand and a guard, and a length that is a uint32. A read is checked: an index below zero, or not below the length, skips the statement it stands in (or makes the guard false) and raises error.execution, which the document counts in `refusals`; no backend reads past the end or, with a negative index, from the other end. A length taken from is checked too: `len(picked) - 1` of an empty list is an unsigned underflow, not a wrapped number. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: an empty list holds no first element
nor a last one: len(picked) - 1 is an unsigned underflow, and no backend reads from the other end
a length is a uint32, so taking one off an empty list is a failure and `count` keeps what it held
0 < len(picked) is false, and no failure: a length compared with a signed cursor is a number
the guard compares picked[0] with picked[1], which a list of one does not have: it is false and says so, and the unguarded `compare` answers instead
9 < 10 holds, so the guarded `compare` is taken
the last element, by an index computed from the length
picked[cursor - 1] with the cursor at 0 is index -1: the statement is skipped and the cursor does not move
the cursor has reached the length
index 3 is not below the length 3: nothing is read, and the cursor stays where it was
emptied, the list has nothing at the cursor
